bullets.title: Anthropic AI models restricted by US government order; Amazon CEO involvement reported
bullets.body: The US government ordered Anthropic to block all foreign nationals from accessing Mythos 5 and Fable 5 models, citing national security concerns. WSJ reports Amazon CEO Andy Jassy's conversations with Trump administration officials triggered the crackdown. Anthropic said it had to disable access immediately, with foreign employees and non-US entities impacted; Microsoft is reportedly restricting employee use of Claude Fable over data retention concerns.

bullets.title: Anthropic/AI export controls: bearish for frontier AI TAM, bullish for sovereign AI buildout and infra
bullets.body: Multiple fintwit accounts are debating the market implications: the bear case is that US export controls shrink the frontier AI TAM and delay model releases 3-6 months; the bull case is that restrictions accelerate sovereign AI buildout globally and increase government AI infrastructure spending. One analyst argues 'Anthropic news is bullish for the AI trade—accelerates sovereign AI buildouts globally.' Others warn this formalizes a model-layer regulatory framework and will force enterprises into multi-model diversification.

bullets.title: NVDA flat for ~10 months despite biggest tech run since 1990s
bullets.body: Multiple posts note NVDA has been essentially unchanged for close to 10 months despite the broader AI/tech bull market, with the CEO Jensen Huang frequently appearing on stage. One poster notes NVDA's market cap now exceeds the entire French stock market. Separately, NVDA pivots to CPUs for China sales after GPU export restrictions, and delivers day-1 support for DeepMind's DiffusionGemma on RTX and DGX platforms.

bullets.title: AMD attacks NVDA: claims EPYC Turin 2.37x better than Vera in agentic AI; Citi upgrades AMD to Buy
bullets.body: AMD claims EPYC Turin delivers 2.37x performance vs NVIDIA Vera in agentic AI workloads, with Zen 6 Venice extending to 3.3x. AMD also boasts '15 out of 15' top CPU spots on Amazon. Citi upgraded AMD to Buy from Hold, raising PT to $575 from $460. Separately, AMD launches $3,999 Ryzen AI Halo PC to undercut NVIDIA's $4,679 DGX Spark.

bullets.title: Hyperscaler leverage doubles to 1.8x; AI debt issuance surges 47% YTD
bullets.body: Fintwit notes hyperscaler leverage (AMZN, GOOGL, META, MSFT, ORCL) doubled from 0.9x to 1.8x in just 6 months, rising 0.3x per quarter. YTD debt issuance is up 47% vs. all of 2024 ($159B vs $108B), and hyperscaler spreads have widened from AA to A. One poster flags $1.8T in off-balance-sheet obligations (purchase commitments, leases) and calls out 12 junk-bond data center deals YTD vs just 4 in all of 2025.

bullets.title: ORCL: Q4 beats on EPS and revenue; massive $638B AI backlog but guides FY27 capex $90-95B and plans $40B debt/equity raise
bullets.body: Oracle Q4: adj. EPS $2.11 vs $1.97 est., adj. revenue $19.18B vs $19.09B est. AI backlog surged to $638B from $138B YoY. The company guides FY27 capex to $90-95B and warned of ~$40B in debt/equity financing—stock fell ~11% on the raise announcement. One analyst noted 'ORCL also didn't raise its FY2027 revenue guidance, keeping it flat at $90B.'

bullets.title: Roku exploring strategic options including potential sale per Reuters
bullets.body: Roku is reportedly exploring strategic options including a possible sale of the company per Reuters. Multiple fintwit accounts are gaming out potential acquirers, with Fox, Netflix, and Comcast among names discussed. The question framed by one analyst: 'Who becomes streaming's gatekeeper?'

bullets.title: Iran-US deal signed Sunday; Strait of Hormuz to reopen—geopolitical event with macro implications
bullets.body: Trump announced an Iran peace deal is scheduled to be signed Sunday, with the Strait of Hormuz to open to all shipping immediately after signing. Trump said no money will exchange hands. Polymarket shows 83% probability of ceasefire by year-end. Oil fell on the news. Separately, Iranian hardliners and some parliamentarians pushed back against the deal framework, and Iran's foreign ministry signaled the MOU is not a final nuclear agreement.

bullets.title: US CPI May: headline meets 4.2% est; core beats at 0.2% vs 0.3% est—car insurance surprise
bullets.body: May CPI came in at 4.2% YoY (highest since April 2023) matching consensus, but core was softer at 0.2% MoM vs 0.3% expected. The core miss was entirely driven by a 1.7% MoM plunge in car insurance (biggest drop since COVID). Super-core ran at 5.2% annualized over March-May; shelter inflation bottomed in February and is now re-accelerating. JPMorgan called May the 'high water mark' and expects Fed to hold.

bullets.title: SpaceX IPO: 4x+ oversubscribed at $1.75T; 2x leveraged ETFs launching Monday
bullets.body: SpaceX IPO priced at $135/share, reportedly 4x oversubscribed with $250B+ in demand including $5B+ from BlackRock and billions from Gulf sovereign wealth funds. SpaceX's AI1 satellite program (Nvidia Rubin GPUs to orbit) and TeraFab chip factory vision are additional catalysts. Morningstar bears value SPCX at a max of $63/share. 2x Long ($SPCH) and Short ($SSPC) SpaceX ETFs launching Monday. SpaceX market cap now exceeds Tesla's.

bullets.title: ECB hikes 25bps to 2.25%—first hike since 2023; cuts growth, raises inflation forecasts
bullets.body: The ECB raised deposit facility rate to 2.25%, the first hike since 2023, citing broadening inflation and Middle East energy shock. ECB cut 2026 GDP forecast to 0.8% and raised 2026 inflation to 3.0% from 2.6%. Lagarde flagged upside inflation risks, no pre-set rate path, and noted the decision was unanimous.

bullets.title: PPI May: +1.1% MoM (vs 0.7% est); headline 6.5% YoY—goods surge record; core PCE expected at 0.35%
bullets.body: May PPI came in at +1.1% MoM, far above the 0.7% consensus, with the headline 6.5% YoY. Final demand goods posted the largest monthly increase on record (+2.8%). Portfolio management services drove 40%+ of the services component. UBS nudged core PCE estimate to 0.35% MoM from 0.27%. Core PPI was softer at 0.4% vs 0.5% est.

bullets.title: Tech sector enters correction (-10.5% from highs); NDX dispersion rivals dot-com era
bullets.body: The Technology sector (XLK) fell approximately 12% in a week, with the dead-cat bounce fading. NDX intraday trading range hit its largest in 3 years outside the April 2025 shock window per Goldman. Tech stock dispersion is at its 2nd-highest level in history, just behind the dot-com bubble. Goldman warns CTAs are sellers in all scenarios and liquidity is suppressed.

bullets.title: LITE CEO confirms CPO/NPO on track; NVDA refutes 800V/CPO delay reports
bullets.body: Lumentum CEO Michael Hurlston confirmed at Mizuho conference that the company is on pace to meet or exceed the top-end of guidance, and that NVDA CPO scale-out and scale-up timelines are confirmed. He also said the NPO opportunity 'is frankly bigger than CPO.' NVDA's Networking SVP separately denied reports of CPO and 800V delays, and Morgan Stanley's Computex checks also found no evidence of pushbacks.

bullets.title: AAOI, COHR, CIEN: photonics selloff from SemiAnalysis CPO delay report viewed as overdone
bullets.body: SemiAnalysis published analysis suggesting CPO scale-up was delayed to 2028+, triggering a broad photonics selloff. Multiple fintwit accounts disagreed: AAOI CFO conducting investor meetings with Street estimates below company capacity plans; one trader called the low-160s a 'clear buying opportunity.' COHR flagged as photonics blue chip with $1.4B pluggable segment growing 40%+. CIEN's CEO seen as positioning the company for major growth.

bullets.title: MSFT Xbox strategic pivot: potential spin-off not ruled out; layoffs planned
bullets.body: Microsoft has not ruled out spinning off Xbox per Bloomberg. Xbox's new CEO Asha Sharma signals the platform may need third-party exclusives and M&A to compete. Xbox planning major layoffs post-June 30 fiscal year close. Satya Nadella says the company is shifting Xbox toward sustainability and monetization after 25 years.

bullets.title: TSLA: GLJ maintains Sell at $24.86 PT; SpaceX/Tesla merger seen 80% probable by 2027
bullets.body: GLJ Research's Gordon Johnson maintains a Sell rating on TSLA, citing Q2 deliveries expected to improve due to inventory clearing but underlying weakness persisting. Separately, DivesTech on CNBC put an 80% probability on a SpaceX/Tesla merger by 2027. Tesla's FSD Supervised approved in Denmark.

bullets.title: SMCI: $7B equity/equity-linked offering announced; $39B AI server orders flagged but authenticity questioned
bullets.body: Super Micro filed for a $7B mixed securities shelf offering, with stock falling ~17-25% on the announcement. One poster noted SMCI received $39B in orders for AI servers in recent weeks but questioned whether they came via an SPV. SMCI down 25% at one point during the week.

bullets.title: BofA double-upgrades INTC to Buy from Underperform with $135 PT; Intel 14A confirmed as foundry crown jewel
bullets.body: Bank of America double-upgraded Intel to Buy from Underperform, raising PT to $135. BofA also raised its 2030 server CPU TAM forecast to $170B+ (from $125B) on agentic AI demand. Intel doubles down on 14A with a Cadence multi-year co-optimization deal. Separately, Intel's 'Project Firefly' ultra-slim 12.9mm laptop design was unveiled.

bullets.title: Burry buys ADBE near historical low P/E ~11; market punishing non-AI profitable companies
bullets.body: Burry reportedly initiated PYPL at $49 and continues adding. He also holds ADBE trading near P/E 11, close to historical lows. His thesis: markets are punishing large, established businesses with real earnings, low debt, and buybacks while capital flows chase AI-narrative names. One fintwit account framed this as 'deep value' vs. mispricings created by AI capital flows.
